newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives can still win again -Mawhinney.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives can still win again -Mawhinney.

text.p: Brian Mawhinney, chairman of the ruling Conservatives, said on Friday the party can still win a fifth consecutive general election despite what he called a "disappointing" performance in a by-election on Thursday.
The opposition Labour Party won the Wirral South by-election with a majority of almost 8,000 votes, registering a 17 percent swing from the Conservatives.
But Mawhinney told BBC radio victory was still in the Conservatives' sights when a general election, widely expected on May 1, takes place.
"We can do it because all of the phoney war is now behind us," Mawhinney said. "Now people are going to focus on who will govern Britain into the next millennium."

Mawhinney said a "by-election culture" had grown up in Britain, in which people who sympathised with large parts of the government's programme voted against it in protest against those policy items with which they disagreed.
But in general elections, people's calculations were very different.

"We had many Tories (in Wirral) saying they are not going to vote for us this time, but when the general election comes, of course they would be voting Tory again," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
